paper.title: Grounding Open-Domain Instructions to Automate Web Support Tasks
paper.central_claim: A general-purpose interactive web agent can execute unseen service tasks from open-domain step-by-step instructions using a typed ThingTalk parser, grounding model and browser runtime; 76.7% single-instruction action accuracy beats direct models and users prefer russ to web navigation.

provenance.actual_model_source: Environment explicitly reports gpt-6.1-sol; no model probing performed.

No score/rating changed; all replacements are atomic and restricted to this seat attempt.

evidence.quote: russ achieves 76.7 % end-to-end accuracy predicting agent actions from single instructions.
evidence.support_explanation: Central 76.7 figure is per-instruction prediction, not complete-task online success.

evidence.quote: we semantically parse natural language instructions to formal actions that support web navigation as well as user interactivity.
evidence.support_explanation: Publication-time design delta over direct element mapping.

evidence.quote: To translate natural language instructions into ThingTalk, we use the previously proposed BERT-LSTM model
evidence.support_explanation: Inherited parser architecture, not a new neural model.

evidence.quote: It filters elements by their type and absolute location. Next it handles relative positioning
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit constraints before neural text similarity.

evidence.quote: It passes the text of the remaining candidates through a Sentence-BERT
evidence.support_explanation: Grounding uses pretrained text embeddings and DOM candidates.

evidence.quote: russ starts a new automated Chrome session for each task and uses Puppeteer to automate web actions in the browser.
evidence.support_explanation: Executable browser runtime exists; does not turn static dataset metrics into live task rates.

evidence.quote: For @ask actions, russ uses a preprogrammed dialogue to ask the user for a dictionary key
evidence.support_explanation: Programmed user interaction rather than learned uncertainty-based assistance.

evidence.quote: Steps found missing from the instructions were inserted. If an instruction mapped to several actions, the text was broken into individual instructions.
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmark uses human-edited step-level instructions, not untouched open-domain plans.

evidence.quote: 304 instructions from 30 tasks in the dev set and 437 instructions from 50 tasks in the test set.
evidence.support_explanation: Task-level dev/test denominator; evaluation not training.

evidence.quote: a Synthetic Dataset with 1.5M training samples.
evidence.support_explanation: Template supervision scale, no self-improvement loop.

evidence.quote:
russ (1.5M training parses) | 87.0%
Ablations | Accuracy (dev)
russ (1.5M training parses) | 88.2%
− - entity extraction | 77.6%
− - 1M training parses, entity extraction | 70.0%
evidence.support_explanation: Parser results and confounded second ablation; abstract summary differs from actual test table.

evidence.quote:
russ | 63.6%
End-to-End Baseline | 51.1%
PhraseNode | 46.5%
evidence.support_explanation: Grounding subtask on 252 element-referring test instructions; not the overall 76.7 metric.

evidence.quote: Had the semantic parser been correct 100% of the time, the Grounding Model would achieve an accuracy of 73.0%.
evidence.support_explanation: Gold-parse oracle estimate reveals cascading error and differs from abstract grounding summary.

evidence.quote: The webpage features used as inputs in PhraseNode are a subset of our representation.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline privilege/features mismatch limits architectural attribution.

evidence.quote: approximately 7 hours on an NVIDIA Tesla V100. russ can perform a new task on-the-job by running the instructions through the semantic parser in less than 1 minute.
evidence.support_explanation: Training and rough parser runtime disclosed, not full latency distribution.

evidence.quote: We recruited 12 participants who were asked to complete 5 customer-support tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Small live user study denominator.

evidence.quote: Participants were able to complete 85% of the tasks on their own on the web and 98% of tasks with the help of russ .
evidence.support_explanation: Human-assisted live task outcome evidence, not autonomous whole-benchmark rate.

evidence.quote: we used Latin Square Balancing
evidence.support_explanation: Counterbalancing reduces ordering effects in user comparison.

evidence.quote: russ gives the user 3 tries to return an expected response before terminating. russ also times out if a webpage takes more than >60 seconds to load in Puppeteer.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit failure boundaries; failures appeared in user study.

evidence.quote: “click the hamburger menu icon”), which is not supported by russ .
evidence.support_explanation: Visual/icon limitation despite open-domain rhetoric.

gap.author_gap: Bridge natural service-help instructions, compositional element descriptions and user dialogue to executable browser actions without bespoke domain APIs or user demonstrations.
gap.checked_gap: 2021 help instructions contain compositional descriptions and interactive user data needs not captured by direct phrase-to-element mapping. Typed retrieval constraints and small live study address a concrete gap, while direct baseline privilege mismatch and edited instructions prevent broad superiority.
gap.residue: Map compositional natural help language to grounded browser actions plus user interaction without bespoke API/task demonstrations.
gap.stakes: Customer-support navigation burdens users; incorrect target selection and missing inputs break execution.
gap.method_response: ThingTalk semantic parser plus DOM type/spatial filtering,Sentence-BERTgrounding and Puppeteer/dialogue runtime; syntheticNL/programtraining.
gap.remaining_gap: No universal untouched-instruction success, weak parser-grounder attribution, image-only controls/dropdowns unsupported, small live-study scope and no longitudinal transfer.
unresolved: Cannot independently settle closest historical original priority; paper own novelty wording broader than audited evidence.
Human-study preference response denominator not specified; text summary and table parser/grounder figures differ.
